          Premier League Match Predictions: The Opta Supercomputer's Picks for This Week
        
      
                          
                      Oct 8, 2026
          
                      Chloe Horswill / Author, Harry Carr / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
With the help of the Opta supercomputer, we provide our Premier League match predictions for Matchday 6 of the 2026-27 season.
With the return of Premier League action following the international break, the Opta supercomputer has delivered its match predictions ahead of the latest weekend of the 2026-27 season.
Manchester City are the only team with a 100% record after Arsenal were thumped 3-0 by Brighton & Hove Albion, who are flying high in third, on MD5.
Brentford, Leeds United, Liverpool and Everton are the other unbeaten clubs, while at the other end, Tottenham Hotspur prop up the table.

Roberto De Zerbi’s side are still yet to win in the Premier League this term – though they did get their first league goals of the campaign in their 3-2 loss to Aston Villa. Fulham and Bournemouth are also yet to win, while Coventry City got off the mark before the hiatus.
Matchday 6 sees fixtures take place on Saturday, Sunday and Monday across a bumper weekend.
Ahead of what should be another intriguing group of Premier League fixtures, let's check out the Opta supercomputer's match predictions.
Arsenal get the Premier League action back underway on Saturday, looking to bounce back from their disappointing loss to Brighton against Leeds United.

That was their heaviest defeat since May 2023 (also 3-0 vs Brighton), but since the start of 2024, the Gunners have only lost back-to-back Premier League games once (in April 2026), with this being their 100th league game since then.

The good news for Arsenal is that they have won nine of their last 10 Premier League games against Leeds (D1), including each of the last seven, while the Whites have won just one of their last 17 away league games against the reigning top-flight champions (D6 L10).

Arsenal are our predictive model’s most confident pick of MD6, with a 68.9% win probability to Leeds’ 13.7%, but Saturday's visitors have started a league campaign unbeaten in five matches (W2 D3) for the first time since their promotion-winning campaign of 2019-20.

Mikel Arteta – who signed a three-year contract extension with Arsenal this week – has won all four of his Premier League games against Daniel Farke, his joint-best 100%-win rate against a manager in the top flight (level with Gary O’Neil), and the German’s worst 100% loss rate against any manager during his career in England.
In the 15:00 kick-offs, Brentford (26.2%) are looking to continue their fine start away to Aston Villa (47.8%), who finally got their first league win against Spurs.

Brentford have kicked off a league campaign unbeaten in five games (W2 D3) for the first time since 2013-14 in League One, last having a longer unbeaten streak at the start of a season in 2006-07 (first seven in the third tier).
They’re unbeaten in their last seven top-flight matches (W2 D5) overall and are looking for a third straight Premier League win over Villa, after doing the double over them last term.
But the Villans have lost just one of their last 11 home league games against Brentford (W4 D6), though that was a 1-0 defeat in this exact fixture last season.
Villa have recorded the fewest shots (48), shots on target (12) and touches in the opposition box (81) in 2026-27, stats Unai Emery will be keen to improve upon.
It has been a tumultuous start for Xabi Alonso at Chelsea, who are looking to end their three-match winless streak in all competitions against Bournemouth.

Chelsea’s five league games under Alonso have seen 22 total goals (10 for, 12 against), and they are the first team to score 10+ goals and concede 10+ goals across that span of matches in a Premier League campaign.
The Blues, who are given a 51.8% win likelihood, are unbeaten in their last nine top-flight meetings with Bournemouth (W4 D5), with each of the last three ending level (22.9% chance of another draw).
